title: The Chess Players
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Narrator
cast.description: Ironic, measured storyteller with a satirical edge

cast.name: Mirza Sajjad Ali
cast.description: Lucknow nobleman, middle-aged, refined, touchy about his pride

cast.name: Mir Roshan Ali
cast.description: Lucknow nobleman, middle-aged, lively, quick to insult

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Urdu tradition. It was written in 1924 by Munshi Premchand. It is called... The Chess Players.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [wry] Lucknow, under Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, is a city of poetry, dance, kite-flying and pleasure. Nobody takes the affairs of state seriously.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mirza Sajjad Ali and Mir Roshan Ali are two minor noblemen whose whole world is a chessboard. They play from breakfast until midnight. Meals go cold. Servants grumble.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] Mirza's wife, tired of a husband who forgets her, has the pieces thrown out. So the game moves to Mir's house... where Mir's wife is perfectly happy to have her husband occupied, for her own reasons.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When an officer comes with a summons to serve in the Nawab's army, the two friends panic.

lines.speaker: mir
lines.text: [alarmed whisper] Mirza Sahib! They want us for the army!

lines.speaker: mirza
lines.text: [hurried] Pack the board. We'll go where no one can find us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They slip out to an abandoned mosque on the far bank of the Gomti. Day after day, they cross the river to play among the ruins.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [grave] One afternoon, a column of East India Company soldiers marches past on the road below. The kingdom of Awadh is being annexed, and its king taken away into exile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [long pause] Not a single sword is raised to stop it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [bitter irony] The two friends watch for a moment... shrug... and go back to the game.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, as the light fades, a quarrel begins over a move.

lines.speaker: mir
lines.text: [accusing] You moved that piece back! You're cheating!

lines.speaker: mirza
lines.text: [offended] Cheating? Your family were grass-cutters before they were ever nobles!

lines.speaker: mir
lines.text: [furious] And yours? Mine at least kept their honour!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [tense] Pride, which could not stir them for their king, stirs them now. They draw their swords and fight... and both fall dead beside the board.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [slowly] Premchand ends on the chess pieces. The two kings sit on their thrones, unmoved... as though mourning the two warriors who died for them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [thoughtful] It is a story about a ruling class too absorbed in its games to notice it was losing everything. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
